proposed.occupation: U.S. Representative for Texas's 29th Congressional District
proposed.summary: Sylvia Garcia is a Democrat who has represented Texas's 29th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2019. Before that she served in the Texas Senate from 2013 to 2018. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 58.2% of the vote and faces Republican Martha Fierro in the November 3, 2026 general election.

positions.stance: Says she is fighting for an economy that works for everyone, not just those at the top, and for lower costs so families have a safe, stable and affordable place to live.
Lead sponsor of the Dream and Promise Act, which would create a path to citizenship for Dreamers and TPS recipients. Supported expanding TPS to Venezuelans and renewing TPS for Central Americans.
Says she has championed funding for community health centers, school-based clinics and mobile health pods to expand access to health care across the district.
Says she helped secure more than $1 billion for a hydrogen hub on the Houston Ship Channel. Was primary sponsor of the Energy Security and Lightering Independence Act of 2021, which was enacted.
Says she secured funding for workforce training programs in Pasadena ISD.

Sponsored the I Am Vanessa Guillen Act, which changed military justice procedures for sexual harassment and assault cases. Sponsored the Don't Block Our Communities Act to fine railroads for trains stopped in neighborhoods.
Says women's freedoms are under attack, especially in Texas, and that she opposes efforts to restrict women's rights.

proposed.summary: Rhonda Hart is a U.S. Army veteran (2000–2003) and gun-safety advocate who began her advocacy after her 14-year-old daughter, Kimberly Vaughan, was killed in the 2018 Santa Fe High School shooting. She ran for Congress in Texas' 14th District in 2024 and lost. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for Texas' 36th District with 64.2% of the vote over Doug Rogers and faces incumbent Republican Brian Babin on November 3, 2026.

positions.stance: Calls for ICE reform and says the agency operates with masks, no body cameras and little accountability. Says "no human being is illegal" and refuses to use that term.
Proposes ending what she calls chaotic tariffs, taxing billionaires and raising the minimum wage to lower the cost of living.
Says health care should be affordable and accessible and not tied to a paycheck. Criticizes Babin's vote for the "Big Beautiful Bill", which she says cut Medicaid.

Opposes sending troops into what she calls unnecessary wars in the Middle East. Supports reversing the ban on transgender troops and more VA funding, based on her own experience as a disabled veteran.
Supports defending a woman's right to choose and passing federal law to codify Roe v. Wade.
Supports safe-storage laws and what she calls common sense gun laws. Says she helped pass the Kimberly Vaughan Safe Storage of Firearms Act as part of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
Opposes school vouchers. Supports more public-school funding and higher pay for teachers and support staff.
Says climate change is a crisis. Supports investing in solar and wind while moving away from fossil fuels gradually, citing their importance to Southeast Texas jobs.
Opposes the SAVE Act. Says voter ID is already required and that requiring a Real ID to vote would amount to a poll tax.
